text:
For forty minutes in Seattle, nobody scored, and for most of the first period it looked like the Kraken were the team that would eventually break through. They out-chanced Chicago 1.40 to 0.85 in expected goals (our measure of chance quality) in the opening twenty, and Spencer Knight had to be sharp early, including a stop on Mackie Samoskevich about a minute in. Then the third period arrived and the Blackhawks found another gear: 2.62 expected goals in the period, more than they had managed in the first two combined.

Cole Smith opened it at 5:58 of the third, tipping in a play started by Ethan Del Mastro and Jordan Greenway. Ninety-four seconds later, Roman Kantserov snapped home a power-play goal off Sam Rinzel and Patrick Kane. That pushed Chicago's win chance from 48% before Smith's goal to 94% after Kantserov's. Jordan Eberle tipped one in at 16:59, his 100th goal with the franchise per Alison Lukan, but Kantserov finished it into the empty net at 19:40.

Kantserov is the story the Blackhawks keep telling right now. He arrived from the KHL after 36 goals in 63 games for Metallurg Magnitogorsk last season, scored his first NHL hat trick against Vancouver on Sunday, and now has five goals in his last two games. He is doing it while Connor Bedard is out injured, which is exactly when Chicago needed someone else to carry the scoring. Rinzel, fresh off a third-star-of-the-week nod, had another assist in 21:30.

Knight was the steady part: 29 saves on 30 shots, 1.74 goals better than the chances he faced, the most wins added of anyone in the building. That was Chicago's third straight win. Seattle went 0 for 4 on the power play, and Lane Lambert called it "not good enough tonight," per Lukan. The Beniers line drove play again, but the Kraken have now lost two in a row and still can't turn possession into goals.
headline: Kantserov keeps scoring, Knight keeps the door shut
